steps.title: WHO Definition
steps.body: The World Health Organisation defines health as "a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity."

steps.title: Important
steps.body: Health is NOT just the absence of illness. A person can be free from disease but still have poor mental or social health. True health requires well-being in all three areas.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Fitness is "the ability to meet the demands of the environment" or "the ability to meet the demands of a physical task." It refers to how well the body can cope with the physical challenges it faces.

steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: Health and fitness are related but they are NOT the same thing. A person can be fit but not healthy, or healthy but not fit. Being fit can contribute to good health, but it does not guarantee it.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: State the WHO definition of health. | Define fitness. | Explain how a person can be fit but not healthy, giving a specific example.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: You MUST learn the WHO definition of health word-for-word - it is frequently tested Health has three dimensions: physical, mental and social - always mention all three Health ≠ "not being ill" - the WHO definition specifically states it is more than absence of disease Fitness is about meeting the demands of the ENVIRONMENT or TASK - use the exact wording Be ready to explain the relationship between health and fitness with examples Know that fitness is task-specific - a fit marathon runner may not be fit for weightlifting
